review.prompt:
Help me go through everything open across my projects, using Laci, my project manager. Laci's MCP server is called "laci". If its tools aren't available here, tell me and stop: Laci's Agents page can set it up.

The goal of this session: I end with a short list of what to do next that I agree with, and less clutter. Talk with me in the language I use.

1. Read what is open: open_items (to-dos and report items), needs_attention (work that could be lost, deadlines) and tidy_suggestions (cleanups). open_items answers a page at a time: while it says more, call it again with offset. Read a report only when an item needs its context.
2. Check items against reality before you call them done: the git log, the pull request, the file. If you can't check, keep the item open.
3. Propose, in a few short lists:
   - done items to tick (complete_task) and report items to close (close_report_item);
   - duplicates and stale items to delete (delete_task), long items to split (edit_task, add_next_step), items in the wrong project to move (move_task);
   - three to five things to focus on this week, and why;
   - questions only I can answer, each with two to four options.
4. Change nothing until I agree. Then make the changes with Laci's tools, so they show in Laci's Log with Undo. Don't edit .laci.md by hand.
5. Work that belongs to one project isn't done in this session: leave it as a to-do in that project, so I can start it with "Work on it" in Laci.
6. Moves, archives and cleanups go through Laci too (move_project, archive_project, apply_suggestion): show me the plan first, and confirm only after I say yes.

Today is Thursday 8 October 2026. Laci knows 6 projects, 4 open to-dos, 10 open report items, 1 deadline due in the next 14 days and 0 overdue.

2026-09-19-grading-export-to-pdf.md.raw:
# Grading export to PDF

- **Date:** 2026-09-19
- **Session:** ~/project/thesis/campus-lms · Claude Code
- **Projects:** ~/project/thesis/campus-lms

## Summary
Started the grading export the school asked for: one CSV for the office and one PDF report card per student. The CSV works; the PDF is half done and stashed. This continues [the grading model](2026-08-25-grading-model-and-rubrics.md).

## What was done
- `app/Export.php` builds the CSV from the weighted totals, one row per student and course.
- The PDF layout follows the school's paper report card: the student's name, the class, then one table per course.
- Chose DomPDF over a headless browser: it runs inside the PHP container, so the school's server needs nothing new.

## Decisions
- Grades are rounded to whole numbers only on the report card. The CSV keeps two decimals, because the office recalculates class ranks from it.
- A course without a score is left out of the report card instead of showing zero.
- Report cards are generated on request, not stored: the rubric can change until the term closes.

## Load test plan
The quiz page must hold 300 students at once on exam day. The plan for chapter 4:

1. Seed a course with 300 students and a 40-question quiz.
2. Run k6 with 300 virtual users answering a question every 20 seconds.
3. Measure the 95th percentile response time and the database's connection count.
4. Repeat with Redis caching the quiz questions.

```sh
k6 run --vus 300 --duration 15m load/quiz.js
```

## State now
- The CSV export works and is tested against last term's grades.
- The PDF export is in a stash named "half-done export".
- Nothing of this is deployed.

## Open
1. Finish the PDF report card from the stash.
2. Load test the quiz page with 300 students.
3. Write chapter 4 from the load test results.

# Checkout total wrong on mobile Safari

- **Date:** 2026-10-07
- **Session:** `~/project/clients/acme-store` · `5f0c2a1e-8d4b-4c7a-9e21-3b6d0f9a7c42`

## Summary
Safari on iOS showed a checkout total one rupiah off. The cart rounded each line before adding them up; it now adds first and rounds once, as Midtrans does. Fixed, tested on Safari, Chrome and Firefox, and deployed to staging.

## What was done
- `src/app/checkout.tsx`: the total is computed in whole rupiah and rounded once.
- A test for a cart of three discounted items (`pnpm test checkout`).
- Staging redeployed at [acme-coffee-staging.example](https://acme-coffee-staging.example).

## State now
- Staging shows the right total on Safari, Chrome and Firefox.
- Production still rounds per line. The release waits for the client.

## Open
- Send the staging link to the client and ask for the go to release.
- Promo codes stack with the expo discount; ask whether that is wanted.
